segments.t: The banquet cake is almost ready in the pastry section, and Louis is proud of it. Barinov comes by to check. Then he spots something in the cream that shouldn't be there. Hear it first, then we'll pick it apart.
Шеф, я почти закончил этот торт.
Я думаю, торт скоро можно подавать.
Это же праздничный торт для гостей!
Сделай красиво, чтобы гости ничего не заметили.
Шеф, я почти закончил этот торт.
'Chef, I have almost finished this cake.' The word
translates to almost, indicating that the pastry chef is nearly done with his long task.
'Show it to me, Louis.' The word
means to show, which is used here as a direct request for the baker to reveal the dessert.
Я думаю, торт скоро можно подавать.
'I think the cake can be served soon.' In this sentence, the expression
stands for soon, suggesting the dessert is nearly ready to be given to the guests.
'Wait, what on earth is this?' The head chef uses the specific command
to tell his colleague to hold on a moment while he examines the strange object.
'Oh, this is an iron clamp!' Here we can clearly hear
which describes the iron material of the heavy tool that ended up inside the cake by mistake.
'Where did it come from in the cream?' Asking about the mysterious origin,
questions where the strange object came from before ending up in the sweet dessert.

'This is a celebration cake for the guests!' To express his massive shock, the boss highlights
to emphasize that this is a special celebration cake meant for very important visitors.
'Probably the little girl was playing here.' Trying to guess what happened, the baker says
meaning probably, as he suspects a little girl was playing around the kitchen area.
'Did Alisa touch your cake?' The boss asks if she
the cake, meaning touched, showing his growing concern about the ruined dessert.
'Chef, calm down, no need to shout.' Hoping to defuse the stressful situation, the baker uses
to tell his boss to remain calm and not raise his voice in anger.
'I will quickly fix everything right now.' Promising to resolve the issue entirely, he says
to assure the boss that he will fix absolutely everything about the ruined dessert immediately.
Сделай красиво, чтобы гости ничего не заметили.
'Make it pretty so the guests notice nothing.' Instructing him to do a proper job, the head chef says
so that the final result looks pretty and the guests will not suspect a thing.
'I promise, the cake will be perfect.' With absolute and complete confidence, the baker states
which means I promise, giving his word that the final dessert will be perfect. This time you'll hear more.

Louis will fix it, and he promises the cake will be perfect. What the guests don't know won't hurt them. Carry on listening, and see you soon.
